title: DeepMind unveils AI system that designs enzymes no living cell ever made
key_facts: Google DeepMind released a preprint for AlphaProtein Novo on 5 Oct 2026, announced on X by Pushmeet Kohli, DeepMind's vice president of science and strategic initiatives; it is a generative model that designs enzymes from scratch rather than tweaking natural ones.

The team built two custom enzymes: one makes piperidine, a six-membered ring found in many drugs, and DeepMind says it does so 99 times faster than the industrial process chemists use today; the other breaks down DEHP, a plastic softener that regulators have flagged for links to reproductive harm and liver damage.
Neither enzyme exists in nature; DeepMind says the system reached state-of-the-art activity on both benchmark reactions it was tested on.

Natural phthalate-degrading enzymes tend to lose activity above room temperature; the article says that if DeepMind's enzyme keeps working when hot it could close a gap that has kept enzymatic plastic breakdown mostly in the lab (the outlet's own reasoning, not a DeepMind result).
The enzyme work was done with external collaborators, including a group at the Francis Crick Institute.
The article stresses that a preprint is not a peer-reviewed paper and a benchmark reaction is not a validated, scaled-up industrial process.
Context given: Isomorphic Labs, DeepMind's drug-discovery spinout, raised $2.1 billion this year; AlphaProtein Novo is a separate research effort.
quote_evidence: Google DeepMind says its new system designed an enzyme that makes a key drug ingredient 99 times faster than the industrial process chemists currently rely on.
A preprint is not a peer-reviewed paper, and a successful benchmark reaction is not the same as a validated, scaled-up industrial process running for months without degrading.
AlphaProtein Novo's enzyme work was done with external collaborators, including a group at the Francis Crick Institute.
why_it_matters_hint: If it holds, enzymes designed to order could cut the cost of making drug ingredients and break down a plastic softener at the high temperatures industry uses; so far it is DeepMind's preprint, not an industrial process.
event_date: Preprint announced on X on 5 Oct 2026.
